title: Perimeter Calculator: Boundary Length on the Map
description: Measure the boundary length of a shape drawn on the map with the Perimeter Calculator — geodesic edge sums in feet, miles and kilometres. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a drawn boundary of four long edges can total 10.75 km (6.68 miles) of perimeter — the fencing, edging and walking distance hiding inside one innocent-looking field.
quick_answer: The Perimeter Calculator measures the total boundary length of a polygon you draw on the map, summing its edges geodesically. Trace the shape and read the perimeter in feet or miles — the number behind fencing estimates, edging orders and boundary walks.

Garden edging, sports-field lines, parking-lot kerbs — all are sold by the metre of boundary, and all begin with this sum.
Rangers, surveyors' assistants and parish boundary-beaters plan the walk from the perimeter: 10.75 km of boundary is a half-day's inspection, not a stroll.

The drawn four-sided parcel from the area examples carries 10.75 km of boundary (6.68 mi) around its 6.08 km². Stretch the same area into a long strip and the perimeter balloons — shape, not size, sets the fence bill.
100 × 150 ft: perimeter 500 ft exactly — 2 × (100 + 150). Simple rectangles check the tool's arithmetic at a glance, which is why they headline the examples.

popular_table.note: Circles have no edges to sum — their boundary is the circumference, 2πr; the radius tools handle that family. Polygons are this page's trade.

faq: Each edge is a geodesic (great-circle) segment between consecutive vertices, and the perimeter is their sum — with the closing edge from the last vertex back to the first included.
Does the calculator close the shape automatically?
Yes — the boundary is a loop by definition. If your shape is an open path (a trail, a coastline stretch), the Trail Distance Estimator measures open lines instead.
Gates and gaps in a fence?
Subtract them after: a 500 ft boundary with two 4-ft gates needs 492 ft of fencing. The perimeter is the gross figure every net figure starts from.
Approximate curves with more vertices — each added point tightens the sum toward the true curve, the same convergence habit as trail tracing.
Slope — is the boundary longer on hills?
Map perimeter is horizontal (plan) length, matching deeds and fence plans drawn on paper. Fencers on steep ground order a margin for the slope's extra run.
Feet for US construction, metres nearly everywhere else — the calculator speaks both so the lumber order and the permit agree.
Perimeter of a circle on the map?
Draw a many-sided polygon to approximate it, or compute 2πr directly with the radius family — the Circle Circumference tools live one click away in the related list.

Coastlines grow with measurement fineness (the famous paradox), so a coastline 'perimeter' must always quote its vertex spacing. Field and parcel boundaries, being legally straight segments, are mercifully finite.
